lines: Barclays' Alex Altmann argues the AI trade is in a 'denial phase': sentiment stays overwhelmingly bullish even as financing stress builds at the edges of the build-out.

He sees a widening split between cash-rich hyperscalers and peripheral 'neoclouds' that are finding debt markets harder to tap, as AI capex — potentially reaching around 12% of GDP by some projections — competes for finite capital.

Altmann describes a 'KOSPI-fication' of the S&P 500, with roughly 75% of expected earnings growth concentrated in semiconductors and the wider AI ecosystem, and says the shifting beta of the 'AI factor' makes it hard for multi-manager funds to hedge.
He notes semiconductor stocks trade on very low multiples (he cites about 3x P/E), signaling investors believe the sector is at a cyclical peak rather than a secular inflection.

In his view, the next leg up needs a killer consumer application, since enterprise revenue alone can't justify multi-trillion-dollar valuations, while running large models locally on consumer hardware could reduce reliance on centralized data centers.
title: What Wall Street Really Thinks About the AI Trade Now
